title: The day nylons went on sale
hook: Within days of their 1940 launch, American women bought nylons by the million.
peek: DuPont's new fibre, nylon, reached American shops as stockings on 15 May 1940. Millions of pairs sold within days, and 64 million in the first year. When wartime shortages ended, queues for nylons were so long the press called them nylon riots.
lede: On 15 May 1940, nylon stockings went on sale across the United States for the first time. DuPont had made nylon in its laboratories in the 1930s, the first fully synthetic fibre to be widely sold, and stockings were its big launch. Shoppers queued outside stores, millions of pairs sold within days, and about 64 million pairs sold in the first year.

bullets.text: Nylon came out of a research team at DuPont led by the chemist Wallace Carothers, who made the key polymer in 1935. The first nylon product on sale was a toothbrush with nylon bristles in 1938, and stockings followed.

The national launch on 15 May 1940 became known as N-Day. Shops limited how many pairs each customer could buy, and many sold out quickly. Nylons were cheaper and tougher than silk stockings, which had dominated before.

In 1942 DuPont turned its nylon over to the war effort for parachutes and other gear. With stockings scarce, some women coloured their legs with leg makeup and drew a seam down the back with an eyebrow pencil.

When nylons returned after the war, crowds overwhelmed shops. In Pittsburgh in 1946, around 40,000 people reportedly lined up for about 13,000 pairs. Newspapers called these scenes the nylon riots, though most were simply enormous queues.
A popular story says nylon stands for New York and London. DuPont said the name was simply coined, reportedly starting from the idea of "no-run" and then changed until it sounded right.
